title: Kubernetes Storage: CSI, StorageClasses, PVCs & StatefulSets
summary: Master container storage interfaces (CSI): dynamic StorageClass provisioning, volumeBindingMode (WaitForFirstConsumer), access modes (RWO, RWX), PersistentVolumeClaims, and StatefulSets with persistent volumeClaimTemplates.
learningObjectives: Configure StorageClasses with CSI provisioners, mount options, and volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer to prevent zonal scheduling deadlocks.
Provision and bind PersistentVolumeClaims with distinct access modes (ReadWriteOnce, ReadWriteMany) and attach them to Pod workloads.
Orchestrate stateful workloads using StatefulSets with volumeClaimTemplates, verifying stable network identity and ordinal storage persistence.

curriculumModules.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI) Architecture & StorageClasses
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: CSI standardizes out-of-tree storage plugins across cloud providers and SAN/NAS systems. StorageClasses define volume drivers, reclaimPolicies (Delete, Retain), allowVolumeExpansion, and volumeBindingMode (Immediate vs WaitForFirstConsumer).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Always configure volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer in multi-AZ clusters so storage volumes are provisioned in the exact Availability Zone where the scheduler places the consuming Pod.

curriculumModules.title: PersistentVolumes, Claims & Volume Access Modes
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: PersistentVolumes (PV) represent provisioned physical storage. PersistentVolumeClaims (PVC) are consumer requests specifying accessModes (ReadWriteOnce, ReadWriteMany, ReadOnlyMany) and capacity requests. Kubelet mounts volumes into container filesystems at target mountPaths.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use ReadWriteOnce (RWO) with block/EBS/pd-ssd for databases to avoid filesystem corruption, and ReadWriteMany (RWX) backed by NFS/CephFS/EFS only for shared assets.

curriculumModules.title: StatefulSets, VolumeClaimTemplates & Ordinal Persistence
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: StatefulSets manage stateful applications requiring ordered deployment, ordinal naming (pod-0, pod-1), and persistent storage through volumeClaimTemplates. When a stateful pod is deleted, its replacement reattaches the exact same PVC and underlying volume.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Decouple PVC retention policy (whenDeleted: Retain) on production StatefulSets so accidental workload deletions never destroy underlying data volumes.

labs.title: Dynamic Storage Provisioning: StorageClass, PVC & Pod Mounts
labs.scenario: Create a custom StorageClass fast-nvme configured with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, define a 10Gi PersistentVolumeClaim data-volume in namespace storage-workloads, and mount the volume into a batch processing Pod data-writer at /mnt/data.
labs.productionContext: Dynamic volume provisioning automates cloud block storage creation upon PVC submission, eliminating manual administrator provisioning tickets.
objectives: Create cluster-scoped StorageClass fast-nvme with WaitForFirstConsumer binding
Deploy Pod data-writer mounting data-volume to /mnt/data
Verify Pod reaches Running status with mounted storage

validationRules.name: fast-nvme
validationRules.remediation: Set volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer in StorageClass fast-nvme.

validationRules.name: data-volume
validationRules.remediation: Apply PersistentVolumeClaim data-volume in namespace storage-workloads.

validationRules.description: Mounted data-volume into Pod data-writer volumes
validationRules.name: data-writer
validationRules.remediation: Attach persistentVolumeClaim data-volume in spec.volumes of Pod data-writer.

validationRules.description: Verified Pod data-writer reaches Running status
validationRules.name: data-writer

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-nvme
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer" > /home/learner/storageclass.yaml

echo -e "apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-volume
  namespace: storage-workloads
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-nvme
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi" > /home/learner/pvc.yaml

echo -e "apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: data-writer
  namespace: storage-workloads
spec:
  containers:
  - name: writer
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: storage
      mountPath: /mnt/data
  volumes:
  - name: storage
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data-volume" > /home/learner/pod-writer.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure StorageClass fast-nvme has volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer, PVC data-volume exists in storage-workloads, and Pod data-writer mounts it.

labs.title: Stateful Workloads: StatefulSet with Ordinal VolumeClaimTemplates
labs.scenario: Deploy an HA distributed database cluster redis-cluster in namespace stateful-apps using a StatefulSet with 3 replicas, a headless Service redis-headless, and volumeClaimTemplates requesting 5Gi storage per ordinal pod.
labs.productionContext: StatefulSets paired with volumeClaimTemplates guarantee that each replica possesses dedicated persistent storage that automatically rebinds across pod rescheduling and rolling updates.
objectives: Create namespace stateful-apps for stateful workloads
Create headless Service redis-headless with clusterIP None
Verify all 3 ordinal pods (redis-cluster-0, 1, 2) reach Running status

steps.title: Create Stateful Namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace `stateful-apps` using `kubectl create namespace stateful-apps`.

steps.title: Inspect Stateful Pods
steps.instruction: Verify that all 3 ordinal pods (`redis-cluster-0`, `redis-cluster-1`, `redis-cluster-2`) are running.

validationRules.description: Created stateful-apps namespace for stateful workloads
validationRules.name: stateful-apps

validationRules.description: Created headless Service redis-headless in stateful-apps
validationRules.name: redis-headless
validationRules.remediation: Apply Service redis-headless in namespace stateful-apps.

validationRules.description: Configured clusterIP None on headless Service
validationRules.name: redis-headless
validationRules.remediation: Set spec.clusterIP: None on Service redis-headless.

validationRules.name: redis-cluster
validationRules.remediation: Apply StatefulSet redis-cluster in namespace stateful-apps.

validationRules.description: Configured volumeClaimTemplates with 5Gi capacity in StatefulSet
validationRules.name: redis-cluster
validationRules.remediation: Configure volumeClaimTemplates requesting 5Gi in StatefulSet redis-cluster.

validationRules.description: Verified at least 3 stateful ordinal pods running in namespace
validationRules.remediation: Ensure all 3 StatefulSet ordinal pods reach Running state.

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: redis-headless
  namespace: stateful-apps
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: redis-cluster
  ports:
  - port: 6379
    targetPort: 6379" > /home/learner/redis-headless.yaml

echo -e "apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: redis-cluster
  namespace: stateful-apps
spec:
  serviceName: redis-headless
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redis-cluster
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: redis-cluster
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: redis
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 6379
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: redis-data
    spec:
      accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 5Gi" > /home/learner/redis-statefulset.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Verify namespace stateful-apps exists, redis-headless has clusterIP None, and StatefulSet redis-cluster has 3 replicas and volumeClaimTemplates requesting 5Gi.

assessmentQuestions.question: What critical operational problem does setting 'volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer' in a StorageClass solve?
options: (Recommended) It delays persistent disk provisioning until the consuming Pod is scheduled, ensuring the volume is created in the exact Availability Zone where the node resides.
It speeds up disk attachment by bypassing the kube-scheduler completely.
It automatically formats the disk with an encrypted ext4 filesystem on creation.
It enables simultaneous ReadWriteMany access across distinct worker nodes for block devices.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: In multi-zone clusters, default 'Immediate' volume binding creates the storage volume in an arbitrary availability zone before the pod is scheduled. If the scheduler later assigns the pod to a node in a different AZ, the pod fails to start with a volume zone mismatch. 'WaitForFirstConsumer' delays provisioning until the pod's node and zone are chosen.

assessmentQuestions.question: When deleting a StatefulSet replica Pod (e.g. redis-cluster-1), what is the default behavior regarding its associated PersistentVolumeClaim?
options: (Recommended) The PVC is NOT deleted by default; it remains intact and is automatically re-attached when a replacement pod with the same ordinal index is scheduled.
The PVC is immediately destroyed along with all underlying disk data.
The PVC is automatically cloned and assigned to redis-cluster-0.
The PVC is detached and marked with reclaimPolicy: Delete in the root namespace.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: To prevent catastrophic data loss during pod restarts or rolling updates, Kubernetes StatefulSets explicitly do not delete PVCs created via volumeClaimTemplates when pods are terminated. The replacement pod with the exact same ordinal identity re-mounts the pre-existing PVC.
